primer.strongest_challenge: The revised design now selects a schema-independent first-hop checkpoint and transaction-bound comparisons. Its strongest remaining challenge is proving that the source-contract fingerprint represents code actually loaded, rather than files first hashed after replacement or a mixed lazy-import generation; an old process must not acquire a fresh fingerprint that blesses stale cached defaults.
primer.best_alternative: Keep the revised shared classifier and existing transaction owner. Bind the source fingerprint at producer load before cached constants or opaque defaults can diverge, validate loaded-module versus installed-source generation when modules load lazily, and refuse mixed/changed contracts before mutation. Retain pre-extraction capability state in the independent upgrade checkpoint, require confirmation and no identified old hosts, and preserve existing migration ownership. This is better because it closes both the first-hop blind spot and accidental blessing of old cached code without introducing a new locking system. Cost: explicit load-order invariants and conservative restart on producer source changes.
primer.consequence_of_current_path: If fingerprint capture is implemented as a first-operation hash rather than a loaded-code identity, an already-running protected process may bless newly installed files while still using old cached model/lexical defaults. This is an implementation risk to test, not a demonstrated defect in unimplemented code.
